title: Vulnerability analysis of coastal tidal flooding in pekalongan city using composite mapping analysis method

idea.research_question: How can Sentinel-1 flood observations be integrated with land cover and terrain to explain and map coastal tidal-flood vulnerability?
idea.hypothesis: A flood-observation layer combined with terrain and land-cover context can distinguish persistent coastal exposure from event-specific inundation and produce a more interpretable vulnerability map than any single indicator.
idea.mechanism: Sentinel-1 backscatter identifies inundated surfaces; Sentinel-2 supplies land-cover classes; DEM-derived elevation represents topographic exposure. Their spatial alignment supports composite vulnerability scoring and independent field validation.

key_variables.target: Coastal tidal-flood inundation extent and composite vulnerability class

idea.analytical_approach: Multi-date Sentinel-1 flood extraction followed by spatial harmonization with Sentinel-2 land cover, DEM-derived elevation and CHIRPS rainfall; construct a composite mapping-analysis score and evaluate spatial agreement against field observations.
idea.expected_contribution: An interpretable, reproducible coastal-flood vulnerability workflow that preserves the distinction between observed inundation and environmental drivers.
idea.falsification_condition: The integrated model does not improve spatial agreement or stability over the Sentinel-1 inundation layer alone, or the selected predictors do not explain differences in observed vulnerability across the coast.
